description: Deliver Server-owned Slack setup and Connection-unavailability guidance for blocked new Slack launches while preserving canonical readiness, delivery deduplication, and existing execution behavior.

tasks.title: Gate new Slack launches and deliver a deduplicated setup nudge
tasks.description: Carry the full canonical AgentExecutabilityResult and the independent Connection availability state through Slack admission. Gate only new DM launches and channel mention launches after classification, including root mentions and first mentions in unbound channel threads, while leaving existing-session follow-ups unchanged. For Agent-blocked or covered non-disabled Connection-unavailable states, enqueue one required Server-authored UserAction/post_message setup/unavailability nudge with the deterministic dispatch reference slack-setup-nudge:{connectionId}:{identity.AsKey()}, safe caller-visible text, and the correct DM thread, channel-root, or triggering channel-thread target; preserve Disabled's audited-discard path and keep executable and unknown Agents on the existing launch path when the Connection is available. Update the Slack product documentation and extend the DM/channel ingress and outbox specs for resource isolation, delivery convergence, targeting, and state independence.
acceptanceCriteria: A new DM with canonical state not-configured returns the distinct agent_not_configured admission result, a channel-root launch with canonical state not-executable returns agent_not_executable, and a first mention in an unbound channel thread with either blocked state is treated as a new launch; none is admitted as executable Agent work.

The Connection availability gate runs before Agent readiness for new launches and covers enabled Connections with incomplete setup, unhealthy/degraded health including service-offline or backpressure reasons, or an OfflineGapAt; it preserves the existing backpressured response code for backpressure and returns connection_unavailable for other covered states, while Disabled retains its audited-discard response.

An Agent-blocked or non-disabled Connection-unavailable new launch performs its blocking decision before SlackProviderInboxStore.AcceptAsync, thread-history launch-context reads, attachment preparation, workspace provisioning, AgentLauncher invocation, Session grain input, or liveness projection, and creates no provider inbox work, AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, AgentTurn, attachment, or new input/turn on an existing Session.

A blocked DM, channel-root launch, and first mention in an unbound channel thread each create a Server-authored SlackOutboxKinds.UserAction row with post_message payload, stable client message identity, dispatch reference slack-setup-nudge:{connectionId}:{identity.AsKey()}, and triggering conversation; the DM preserves body.ThreadTs, a root launch has no thread target, and an unbound channel-thread launch targets body.ThreadTs.

Setup/unavailability-nudge text states that the Agent or Slack Connection is not ready to accept the task and directs the caller to the responsible owner/operator, while excluding gap codes, detailed health/failure messages, raw configuration, credentials, repair paths, repair commands, Agent-generated wording, and claims that execution started.

Sequential redelivery, concurrent admission, and delivery-uncertain retry/reconciliation for one (workspace team, conversation, message timestamp) and either blocking cause converge on one durable setup-nudge intent and never enqueue a replacement row or second Slack message; the original conversation and thread target remain unchanged.

Existing DM and bound channel-thread follow-ups remain usable when the current Agent readiness or Connection availability is blocked, and their persisted Session snapshots remain unchanged; both gates are checked only for new launch routes.

Executable Agents follow the normal inbox, launch, liveness, and resource-creation flow without a setup nudge when the Connection is available; unknown Agents remain admitted for Runner verification without a setup nudge; Disabled Connections retain their existing audited-discard response without a nudge, while non-disabled unavailable Connections receive the required nudge and are not reported as Agent readiness gaps.

Slack DM and channel ingress specs assert the Agent and Connection admission codes, safe payload, DM/thread/root targeting, resource counts, existing-session behavior, sequential and concurrent deduplication, and delivery-uncertain reuse across unhealthy/service-offline, offline-gap, setup-incomplete, and backpressured states; the outbox reliability assertions cover the existing retry/reconciliation lifecycle.
docs/slack.md documents the setup-mode response, the caller-safe summary, the owner/operator-only readiness detail, and the independence of Agent readiness from Connection health.
The relevant Server test suites pass, including the focused Slack DM/channel ingress and outbox reliability specs.
tasks.output: Updated Slack ingress/readiness dispatch code, a stable setup-nudge outbox producer, expanded Slack ingress and delivery specs, and updated docs/slack.md.
tasks.notes: Use AgentReadinessService as the only Agent readiness authority and keep Connection availability as a separate persisted-state gate with precedence. Reuse EnqueueRequiredAsync and UserAction; no schema migration or new outbox kind is needed. Required insertion remains allowed under outbox backpressure. Resolve a durable accepted replay before applying the new-launch gates so a previously accepted identity is retried through its existing route.

tasks.title: Expose canonical executability in Slack diagnostics and operator surfaces
tasks.description: Project the canonical AgentExecutabilityResult into the authorized Slack Connection diagnostic/read surfaces alongside the existing Connection facts, retaining the legacy Connection AgentReadiness field for compatibility. Ensure operators can inspect the complete Agent state, every gap, next action, and FixEntryPoint from AgentReadinessService/AgentInfo.Executability plus the Connection setup, health, offline-gap, and backpressure facts, while Slack-facing setup/unavailability text remains a fixed safe summary and Connection availability remains separate from Agent executability. Add API and service specs for canonical detail, authorization scoping, availability precedence, and lifecycle independence.
acceptanceCriteria: The authorized Slack Connection diagnostic/read response exposes the canonical executability state, all canonical gaps, each gap's code/message/nextAction/FixEntryPoint, and PendingLaunchNote when present, sourced from the same AgentReadinessService result used by ingress; no Slack-specific readiness calculation is introduced.

The response retains the legacy Connection AgentReadiness field and continues to expose Connection setup progress, desired state, health, and health reason as separate facts rather than replacing them with Agent executability.

API/read-surface specs cover a not-configured Agent with a model-missing gap and a not-executable Agent with an execution-configuration failure, verifying complete canonical details and repair entry points for authorized owners/operators.

Diagnostic precedence and state independence remain intact: Disabled retains its existing audited-discard response, while unhealthy, offline, setup-incomplete, and backpressured non-disabled Connection conditions use the new setup/unavailability nudge mode and their applicable Connection admission responses; an Agent readiness block or Connection-unavailable admission does not mutate DesiredState, SetupProgress, ConnectionHealth, OfflineGapAt, or existing Session history; a Connection health problem is not reported as an Agent gap.

Read-surface tests verify that privileged detail is not copied into the caller-visible setup-nudge payload, including gap codes, detailed failure text, configuration or credential data, repair paths, and commands.
The focused Slack diagnostic, Agent API/read-surface, ConnectionDiagnostic state-matrix, and existing Connection lifecycle tests pass.
tasks.output: Updated Slack diagnostic/read projections with canonical AgentExecutabilityResult details, compatibility-preserving Connection facts, and passing authorization/state-independence tests.
tasks.notes: AgentQuerier already hydrates AgentInfo.Executability for privileged Agent surfaces. Keep that contract canonical and add the Slack diagnostic projection without using persisted AgentConnection.AgentReadiness or AgentReadinessDeriver as a launch verdict.
